dish.title: Salvadoran Bean-and-Cheese Pupusas with Curtido and Salsa Roja
dish.description: Thick masa harina rounds stuffed with smooth refried small red beans and mozzarella and griddled until spotted brown, served with curtido, a tangy slaw of cabbage, carrot, onion, jalapeno, oregano, and cider vinegar, and a simple simmered salsa roja of roma tomatoes, onion, and garlic.

recipe_version.title: Salvadoran Bean-and-Cheese Pupusas with Curtido and Salsa Roja
recipe_version.description: Thick masa harina rounds stuffed with smooth refried small red beans and mozzarella and griddled until spotted brown, served with curtido, a tangy slaw of cabbage, carrot, onion, jalapeno, oregano, and cider vinegar, and a simple simmered salsa roja of roma tomatoes, onion, and garlic.

ingredients.name: white onion
ingredients.note: half thinly sliced for curtido, half for salsa

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: 1 tsp curtido, 1/2 tsp salsa, 1 tsp dough

ingredients.name: masa harina
ingredients.display_name: masa harina whose label lists corn treated with lime

ingredients.name: refried small red beans
ingredients.display_name: vegetarian refried small red beans, puréed smooth (about half a 16-oz can), whose label lists small red beans, water, oil, and salt, no lard

ingredients.name: low-moisture mozzarella
ingredients.display_name: low-moisture mozzarella made with microbial or vegetable rennet

ingredients.name: neutral oil
ingredients.note: for the skillet and your hands

steps.title: Make the curtido
steps.body: Shred the cabbage, grate the carrot, thinly slice half the onion, and slice the jalapeno. Toss in the large bowl with the oregano, vinegar, 1/2 cup water, and 1 tsp salt. It stands through the rest of the recipe (overlap, about 45 minutes), tossed now and then.

steps.title: Make the salsa
steps.body: Blend the tomatoes, the remaining onion half, the garlic, and 1/2 tsp salt until smooth. Simmer in the 1-quart saucepan, stirring now and then, until slightly thickened, about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Mix the dough and filling
steps.body: Stir the masa harina and 1 tsp salt with 1 3/4 cups warm water in the medium bowl and knead until soft and smooth like play dough, about 2 minutes; cover. Mix the 1 cup beans and the mozzarella (about 1 1/2 cups filling).

steps.title: Shape
steps.body: With lightly oiled hands, divide the dough into 8 balls. Press each into a 3-inch cup, fill with 3 tbsp of the bean-cheese mix, close the dough over it, and pat gently into a 4-inch round about 1/2 inch thick, pressing any cracks closed.

steps.title: Griddle
steps.body: Heat the 12-inch cast-iron skillet over medium, about 3 minutes, and wipe it with a little oil. Cook 4 pupusas at a time until spotted golden-brown, about 4 minutes per side. Keep the first batch warm on a plate and repeat (2 batches).

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Serve the pupusas hot with the drained curtido and the salsa roja.

scaling_notes.1: Make a quarter of the dough (1/2 cup masa harina) for 2 pupusas and a quarter of the curtido and salsa; griddle in a 10-inch skillet.
scaling_notes.2: Make half for 4 pupusas; griddle all 4 at once in the 12-inch skillet.
do_not_scale: curtido: it needs about 30 minutes standing at any size

coverage_contribution: Central America has no meal in the catalog, and there is no stuffed masa dish. A vegetarian hands-on dinner.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with venezuelan-black-bean-plantain-arepas: thin stuffed masa harina rounds with curtido, not split cornmeal arepas filled after cooking. Compared with black-bean-quesadillas: the beans and cheese are sealed inside a thick masa dough, not folded in a tortilla. Compared with chipotle-lime-black-bean-bowls: beans sealed in griddled masa with a vinegar slaw, not a rice bowl.
not_duplicate_of: Not gorditas (not split and filled) and not quesadillas.
